sourceAnchors.visualArbitrationNote: Printed page 348 explicitly leaves open why a manic reaction may be clinically absent after melancholia and why mania may appear without a clinically detected melancholic phase. Szondi then advances only an assumption that the other phase may have been present in an abbreviated form and notes that the drive test can show `Ansätze` of a clinically missing phase.

sourceExcerpt: Die Frage, warum in bestimmten Fällen der Melancholie die manische Reaktion fehlen kann und warum die Manie auch ohne eine melancholische Phase sich plötzlich einzustellen vermag, müssen wir vorläufig offen lassen.
romanianRendering: Szondi lasă explicit deschisă problema fazei clinice absente. El adaugă numai ca presupunere că faza opusă ar fi putut exista într-o formă atât de scurtă încât să nu fie observabilă clinic și spune că în Triebversuch pot apărea `Ansätze` ale fazei clinic absente.
doctrinalStatement: Absența clinică a uneia dintre faze rămâne în sursă o problemă `vorläufig offen`. Ipoteza că faza opusă ar fi existat abreviat este introdusă prin `Wir haben aber Grund, anzunehmen` și trebuie păstrată ca ASSUMPTION, nu ca fază latentă obligatoriu reconstruită. Eventualele `Ansätze` din Triebversuch pot susține numai observația source-defined, nu interpolarea automată a unei faze care nu a fost efectiv înregistrată.
conditions: Applies only when discussing clinically absent phases in the source's manisch-depressive longitudinal model.
exceptions: Do not infer a missing melancholic or manic phase merely because the opposite phase is observed.
Do not reconstruct an unobserved phase from a few isolated factor similarities.
Preserve the source's explicit open-question status even when test material shows partial `Ansätze`.
scopeNotes: This record deliberately captures both the open question and Szondi's limited hypothesis so that later longitudinal software cannot silently fill missing phases.
No phase interpolation or hidden-state model is authorized.

relations.note: Limits retrospective inference when a melancholic phase is clinically absent.
Limits retrospective inference when a manic phase is clinically absent.

reviewNotes: Canonical BODY U002514 checked against deterministic P0 evidence; admitted PDF printed page 348 reconsulted.
Kept at ASSUMPTION strength; no automatic missing-phase inference is added.
